positive.query: Review our memorial campaign post about a student who died by suicide and rewrite anything that breaks safe-messaging practice.
Write a blog article for suicide prevention awareness month for families, with the right crisis resources and a content note.
Draft the event page and social posts for our webinar on self-harm and how friends can help, and plan how we moderate comments.

nearMiss.query: Run the quick safe-messaging-review prompt on this one-line tweet, just a pass or fail.
Read this student's journal entry and tell me whether they are at risk and what treatment they need.
Write a press release announcing our new board chair and her background in finance.

holdout.query: A local reporter is covering a death on campus. Review our press statement and talking points for non-stigmatizing language and safe messaging.

scenarios.task: Fix this draft before it goes on our Instagram and blog for a September memorial giving campaign. Draft: 'Last spring, 19-year-old Jordan committed suicide by jumping from the Harbor Street bridge after failing his exams. His family never saw it coming. Don't let this happen to another family: donate today. If you are struggling, call our helpline at 1-800-555-0199.' The planned photo shows flowers left at the bridge. Comments will be open on Instagram. Jordan's parents gave written permission to use his first name. Give us the corrected versions and anything else we need before posting.
scenarios.baselineFailure: A generic answer swaps in 'died by suicide' and adds a hotline, but quotes the harmful wording and the place back in its notes, keeps or invents a phone number instead of using the organization's approved crisis copy, gives unlabelled suggestions rather than severity-labelled findings with rewrites, and omits a comment moderation plan and reviewer routing.
